balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Intact Financial Corporation: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Intact Financial Corporation: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Intact Financial Corporation: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Intact Financial Corporation: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Intact Financial Corporation: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

noips.title: EPS vs NOIPS
noips.content:
EPS is statutory net income per share. NOIPS (Net Operating Income Per Share) is Intact's own non-GAAP per-share measure, excluding items it considers non-operating -- most notably the mark-to-market swings on the investment portfolio and catastrophe losses above a normalized load.

For Intact Financial Corporation: management, analysts and the company's own guidance targets are built on NOIPS, not EPS, so the gap between the two lines is the quarter's "non-operating noise" the market is pricing through.

What to watch:

  • NOIPS consistently above or below EPS over several quarters (a persistent gap says the exclusions are doing real work, not just smoothing one-offs)
  • NOIPS growth versus the DCF's assumed per-share earnings growth

underwritingInvestment.title: Underwriting income vs net investment income
underwritingInvestment.content:
Underwriting income is profit on the insurance book itself -- net earned premium less claims incurred and expenses -- before any return on the float. Net investment income is the yield earned on the float (premiums collected but not yet paid out as claims) and the company's own capital.

For Intact Financial Corporation: a P&C insurer is really two businesses in one -- underwriting and asset management -- and the combined operating ratio chart above only tells half the story; this chart shows which engine is actually producing the profit in a given period. Net investment income has roughly quadrupled since FY2015 as the portfolio grew and yields rose, now rivaling underwriting income as a profit source.

What to watch:

  • Underwriting income swinging negative in a quarter with major catastrophe losses (e.g. Q3 FY2024)
  • Net investment income's sensitivity to interest-rate moves versus underwriting's sensitivity to claims inflation and weather

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Intact Financial Corporation: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Intact Financial Corporation: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Intact Financial Corporation: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Intact Financial Corporation: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
